Hi [~accountid:5bf7a8fb7ffaec527a023256],

According to art. 139.3 of the Public Sector Contracts Act (*“LCSP”*): _A tenderer may submit no more than one submission, without prejudice to Article 142 concerning the admissibility of variants and Article 143 concerning the submission of new prices or values in an electronic auction. Nor may it sign any tender in a joint venture with others if it has done so individually or be in more than one joint venture. Infringement of these rules shall result in the non-admission of all the proposals underwritten by him._

Despite this, the law indirectly permits the participation of related companies in public contracting procedures. This is evident from Article 149.3 of the LCSP, which outlines how to calculate the abnormality of bids when companies from the same group submit offers: _When companies belonging to the same group, within the meaning of Article 42.1 of the Commercial Code, have submitted bids, only the lowest bid will be taken into account for the purposes of applying the system for identifying the bids that are presumed to be abnormal, regardless of whether they submit their bid alone or jointly with another company or companies outside the group and with which they compete in a temporary joint venture._

Therefore, the mere participation of related companies or companies belonging to the same group in the same tender cannot automatically lead to their exclusion. However, Public Administrations are obligated to uphold the principles of equal treatment and free competition (Article 132.3 LCSP). Based on this duty, they could apply the "lifting of the veil" doctrine to assess whether these proposals were actually submitted by the same bidder with a fraudulent purpose. This approach is supported by [Resolution no. 1278/2019 of the TACRC|https://www.iberley.es/resoluciones/resolucion-tacrc-1278-2019-11-11-2019-2350492#google_vignette], which states:

"In these cases, case law allows the appearance of independent personality to be pierced, in order to undo the fictitious and break into reality, which, in a case such as the one analysed, would mean that the bids from two or more companies should be considered as having been formulated by the same bidder".

We also can highlight resolution number 28/2018 of the Administrative Contracting Court of the Autonomous Community of Galicia, which excludes two entities when it verifies that they had the same fax, same administrators and registered office and Resolution 12/2019 of the same Court which analyses a case in which the proposals were sent from the same fax, on the same day and time and by the Post Office using the same office, when only one of these companies had its headquarters in that city.

In conclusion, as a general rule, we can assert that the submission of bids by different related companies or companies within the same corporate group in a tender is permitted. However, the contracting authority must ensure compliance with the principles of equality and free competition. *If evidence and indications suggest that such submissions were made in a coordinated manner to circumvent the law, the exclusion of both bidders is possible under the "lifting of the veil" doctrine.*

Legal recommends not proceeding with applications from two entities. Therefore, unless *both* Ops and PP/Licensing wish to move forward, there is no need to consult outside counsel (also bearing in mind that we have used most of our Legal budget already with litigations in BE and IT).



Many thanks.

+*UPDATE NOTE*+ 

*_research below:_* 

i. There is *no* explicit wording in the General Platform Terms for Drivers pertaining to deduction of wages stemming from Customer Service complaints and subsequent refunds. However, there is wording to suggest that the Journey Fee for drivers is subject to conditions (listed in Section 18(h)) which include driver error and unexpected circumstances and in such cases the Journey Fee can be updated by Bolt. In order to keep this email succinct, I have extracted and highlighted the relevant terms and conditions in a Google Doc linked below:

[Research Task - Deductions from Journey Fees|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ciEkZd6_Lv5GbPFjWUMLTDFwPyiI4XWqK-EwKrrf6f4/edit?usp=drive_web]

ii. It does not appear that self-employed independent contractors have [any|https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/employment-status-and-employment-rights/employment-status-and-rights-checklist-for-employers-and-other-engagers] statutory rights or protections against deductions from wages.

iii. There appear to be no Terms and/or statutory requirements requiring Bolt to proactively notify drivers of deducted earnings. However, drivers do have the right per section 19 of the Terms (on page 2 of the doc above) to request a review of their Journey Fees and dispute them and Bolt has reserved the right to withhold the disputed amounts until after the review/dispute resolution.

{noformat}select distinct
asc2.name as city,

where etl.created_date >= DATE('2021-01-01')
and etl.created_date < DATE('2023-01-01')
and etl.from_vat_code = 'FR87888880671'{noformat}

{noformat}select 
public_id as commission_invoice_id,
invoice_sub_type as invoice_type,
period_start_date,
period_end_date,

# *Predicting trip value*
The €35 fee should be an accurate prediction since most trips are unlikely to last more than one hour. I don't oppose setting a higher pre-authorization if you believe it's safer. # *Who is this catered towards?*
We want to be inclusive of all customers at this time. Business clients present a strong business case for this category as they often require multiple stops in a row to run errands around the city. The hourly fee is much higher than the customized one, and we will charge extra for distance once a certain number of kilometers is reached. This approach will boost driver earnings while providing a personalized experience for riders.

- Launch it only in Lisbon so we can monitor closely what is happening and adjust if needed. - Don't announce the category to riders for now.

Please let us know how we can proceed and what measures can be taken to ensure we can launch it and add value to the market.

Hi,

These cash orders are hidden, as fleet setting are done in this way. 



In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either). The reason why we even create these entries - Finance and Accounting.

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal). In some countries our invoices are not considered to be legal for cash rides (e.g. Hungary).

Second case - the issuer and the recipient are the same. It’s not legal to issue an invoice to oneself so in case the driver's registry code and the rider’s registry code are identical, the invoice will be hidden.

In short, we cannot provide this invoice as it has to be given by the driver

* Audio Recording is in progress. User records a Video from his/her device and ends it. Audio recording in resumed and yellow indicator is present.
* Audio Recording in progress. VOIP CALL received and Accepted by the Driver. Recording is paused now, Rider ends the call. Recording is resumed and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording in progress. VOIP call received and Accept by the Driver. Recording is paused now,  Driver ends the call. Recording is resumed and Yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording in progress. Driver App is in background state. Driver receives VOIP Call and declines it. Audio Recording is still in progress and have yellow indicator on the device
* Audio recording in progress. Driver initiates a VOIP call. Audio Recording is paused. Rider doesn’t accept the call. Recording is resumed again and yellow indicator is present
* Audio recording in progress. Driver initiates a VOIP call. Audio Recording is paused. Rider declines the call. Recording is resumed again and yellow indicator is present
* Audio recording in progress. Driver initiates a VOIP call. Audio Recording is paused. Driver ends the call before rider pick-up the call. Recording is resumed again and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording in progress. Driver app is in background. VOIP CALL received and driver declines it. Audio recording remains in progress and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in progress. Driver receives a B2B order and doesn’t accept it. Audio recording is not interrupted and is working. Yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in progress. Driver Receives B2B order and declines it. Audio Recording is not interrupted and is working. Yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in progress. Driver app is in background state. Driver receives a B2B order and accept it from the notification bar. Audio Recording is not interrupted. Yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in Progress. Driver make a Phone call and the receiver Rejects it. Audio Recording is resume and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in Progress. Driver makes a phone call and received doesn’t pick-up the call. Audio Recording is resume and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in progress. Driver makes a phone call and receiver accept it. Receiver ends the call. Audio Recording is resume and yellow indicator is present
* Audio Recording is in progress. Driver makes a phone call and receiver accepts it. Driver app is in background state. End the call - audio recording is resumed again Yellow indicator is present

Hi all

In this case, the business customer wants to conclude a Data Processing Agreement with us (Annex 2), treating Bolt as a data processor. We cannot accept the status of a data processor as it does not correctly represent the business and data processing arrangements between Bolt and the business customer. Please use the following message to push back:

“_Hi [_]_

_We regret to inform you that Bolt cannot sign the proposed Personal Data Processing Entrustment Agreement attached to the Special Conditions Agreement as Appendix 2, as it does not accurately reflect the business arrangement between Bolt and Medicover, nor the legal roles of Bolt and Medicover as far as data processing is concerned._

_To be clear, Bolt operates as an independent data controller when providing services to its business customers. Our_ +_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+ _Section 4 states explicitly that Bolt and the business customer maintain their independent data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its processing activities and adherence to applicable laws, including the GDPR. This covers areas such as engaging subprocessors, implementing necessary security measures, and establishing data retention periods._

_When a business customer`s employee or any data subject uses Bolt Business services for a ride, they are treated as a regular user of the Bolt Rider App. The experience of these business users is identical to that of regular users, except for the availability of an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride). This may result in a scenario where, if a business customer deactivates and removes a business user's account, this individual will lose access to an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride)._

_However, they will continue to be a customer of Bolt, which means Bolt will keep processing their personal data unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention period specified in_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/] _expires. In practical terms, this means that the personal data provided by business customers is  used to match newly added business users with the accounts of standard users. Individuals remain in control over their data._

_Additionally, as there had been a contractual relationship with the business customer, the data received from the business customer may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from the agreement with the business client. Deleting personal data on the request of business customers may deprive both Bolt and the individual from the opportunity to defend or substantiate their claims in the event that any claims should arise. Therefore, the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller for the above stated purposes unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims) expires, as outlined in the applicable_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/]_._

_Please note that the notion of controllership in our arrangement is cemented by the_[ |https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en][+_EDPB Guidelines 07/2020_+|https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en] _on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR. Specifically, p. 27 para. 82 demonstrates this via “_*_Example: Taxi service”_*_. While Bolt operates as an online platform rather than providing taxi services directly, the example still effectively clarifies the logic underpinning the controller relationship._

_We appreciate your attention and trust that this explanation has clarified any concerns or questions you may have.”_

Hello!

As explained in [Manager's Playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BMP/pages/4427186625/Equity+Compensation] then equity compensation is set as a % of annual base salary, as each job level at Bolt has a specific equity range in place.
Nils is currently holding OM role meaning that his equity comp total value should make 40%-50%-60% (F) of his annual salary. His currently equity ratio is however 97% of his annual salary (37% more than *max* equity range).
If he is now promoted to a senior OM role, then equity ranges would also increase from previous ones mentioned, to higher ones: 65%-75%-90% (G). As you have indicated this his annual salary would change to €84k. With his new annual base salary in place his equity valuation would make 77.4% out of that, meaning that he already vests within the recommended level. Min and mid outcomes of the calculations show negative values as he vests more than these percentages indicate. As mentioned then he's about to fully vest his initial grant on 10th of Aug, 2024. As both his promotion and initial grant fully vesting happens in a very short time then two options could be considered:

# he will be awarded 2 separate grants:

# one grant due to his promotion effective as of 1st of July, 2024, grant date 1st of July 2024
# second grant once his initial grant has fully vested, grant date 11th of Aug 2024

# he will be awarded 1 unified grant for his promotion and initial grant refresh

The outcome of the numbers doesn't necessarily change (unless his salary or job level is changed between July and 11th of Aug).

* If two separate grants are made then with his promotion he could at max be awarded with 46* units in July (soon to be fully vested grant to be included in the calculations), and as a refresh grant he could be awarded with max 26* units in August (soon to be fully vested grant to be excluded from the calculations, but promotional grant needs to be included), totalling 72* units.
* If one grant is made for promotion and refresh, then he could be granted 72* units (as an exception he will receive his refresh grant 1,5 earlier to avoid making 2 separate grants in such a short time).

*All calculations are done with a presumption that given equity ranges are followed. If more units are awarded than mentioned equity ranges indicate, then this should be considered as an exception that the vertical head needs to approve.



Kind regards

Ingrid Valgejarv

Apparently the ANR happens in {{MapStateProviderImpl.postMapEvent}} method when {{mapMovingInteractionsSubject.publish}} is called. According to the stacktrace from Crashlytics, the rx BehaviorRelay is eventually transformed to coroutine flow down in the chain. {{asFlow}} method creates a channel flow and uses {{trySendBlocking}} to emit items. Default channel that is created internally is a buffered one (buffer size is 64 items) and when the buffer is full, {{trySendBlocking}} method blocks the current thread (which in this case is the main thread, hence the ANR).

The question of why the buffer is overflown and if we can do something to avoid it deserves a separate investigation. In the scope of this task, the ANR was fixed by migrating {{BehaviorRelay}} to {{BehaviorFlow}}, which never blocks the emitting thread. This migration was done in [another task|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MP-1549] and is shipped in CA.121.0 version.

*On alpha and credible intervals:*

# Causal Impact evaluates Credible Intervals based on alpha. Alpha is divided by 2. See how percentiles are achieved [here|https://github.com/WillianFuks/tfcausalimpact/blob/6f62c5d19befcaa5faf215417918f9a4cbf5cdac/causalimpact/inferences.py#L49]
# Given we know 
## the value of metric at some percentile (from step 1) AND
## the center of distribution
=> we can calculate the SD
(Causal Impact does it a bit differently [here|https://github.com/WillianFuks/tfcausalimpact/blob/6f62c5d19befcaa5faf215417918f9a4cbf5cdac/causalimpact/summary/templates/summary#L2C100-L2C111], but almost same logic:
### take average between Upper and Lower = (U-L)/2 to get the center of distribution
### divide the result by the z_score.
# From SD we can calculate all other percentiles that we want (assuming that resulting distribution is normal). We make this assumption, because WillianFunks (Python’s CI author also makes it, see [here|https://github.com/WillianFuks/tfcausalimpact/blob/6f62c5d19befcaa5faf215417918f9a4cbf5cdac/causalimpact/summary/templates/summary#L2]).

How we and CI calculate Cred Intervals (not very different in reality:

{noformat}CI
my_df['sd'] = abs(my_df['predicted_upper'] - my_df['predicted_lower']) / (2*norm.ppf(0.95) )
Our version
my_df['sd2'] = abs(my_df['predicted_upper'] - my_df['predicted']) / (norm.ppf(0.95) ){noformat}

Most common percentiles are:

{noformat}norm.ppf(q) takes q as a percentage of total area from the start (not the average)

norm.ppf(0.8)   #0.841
norm.ppf(0.9)   #1.281
norm.ppf(0.95)  #1.644
norm.ppf(0.975) #1.959{noformat}



How to calculate the probability of impact. Assuming that posterior distribution is normal, we can:

{noformat}my_df['prob_of_impact']  = norm.cdf(abs(my_df['actual'] - my_df['predicted']) / my_df['sd']){noformat}

Reviewed the DPA and overall can confirm that no red flags were spotted in terms of regulatory compliance; however, the DPA does not adhere to the absolute majority of our standards.

I am attaching the copy of the agreement [^Master Subscription & Services Agreement - European - Bolt Technology OU_reviewed_Bolt.docx] that I reviewed and made my suggestions to bring the DPA to our standards (where I believe is most reasonable and not to trigger strict pushback, i.e general subprocessor authorisation remains).

I also agree with the points clarified by [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] re/ audit requirements - this is to bring this to our internal standards.

The main risks are the following:

* no concrete timeframes for any of the obligations by Workiva, such as notification of data breaches, data subject requests;
* audits and other obligations by Workiva are to be performed at Bolt`s expense (i.e. support to respond to regulatory consultations or DPIAs);
* general authorisation of subprocessors;
* Workiva reserves the right to engage subprocessors without prior notice  where the reason for the change is outside of Workiva’s reasonable control and prompt replacement is required for security or other urgent reasons - but Workiva remains liable for its subprocessors, and Bolt can still object to their use.
* limitation of liability (same as for the main agreement)

Thanks!

----

As agreed, please find below our advice on French rules on marketing calls and marketing communications (email and SMS) in a Business to Consumer (B2C) context.

Regarding marketing calls, we indicated the new rules directly below. These new rules are in force since March 1^st^, 2023 for the businesses making marketing calls to French consumers. 

# *Marketing emails and SMS*

_As a general principle_, in a B2C context, the *rule is the opt-in* i.e. the recipient must give its prior consent to receive such marketing communications.

_By exception_, the +opt-out regime applies provided the following conditions are met+:

* the recipient's contact details have been collected directly from him/her;
* the recipient has already bought similar products or services to the marketer;
* the direct marketing communication concerns similar products or services provided by the same natural or legal person;
* the recipient was informed of the use of its data for marketing communications; and
* the recipient is offered the possibility to object easily and free of charge to further solicitations at the moment of collection and in each marketing communication.

In any case, all the emails/SMS must:

* specify the identity of the marketer;
* offer a simple and free way for the recipients to object to further solicitations (e.g. an unsubscribe link at the end of the email or SMS or a specific number to oppose within the SMS).

# *Marketing calls*
# +Automated calls+

_By principle_, in a B2C context, the rule is *the opt-in*.

_By exception_, the +opt-out applies+ subject to the same conditions as mentioned above for SMS and emails. 

Since January 2023, it is prohibited to use number stating by 06 or 07 for marketing calls, and specific numbers must be used (as provided by the French authority for electronic communications, the Arcep).

# +Marketing calls made by individuals+

In this context, the opt-out regime is applicable, but the professional calling the consumer must comply with various obligations:

* at the beginning of the call, inform the recipient in a clear, specific and understandable way of:

* its identity or identity of the person for whom he is making the call;
* the commercial nature of the call;
* its right to be on the “do not call” list without any charge. Note that this subscription is for a period of 3 year renewable by tacit reconduction for period of 3 years.

* _(new rule)_ make the call:

* only from Monday to Friday (except if the day is a bank holiday in France) and between 10am and 1pm then between 2pm and 8pm (time zone of consumer). By exception, the trader can make marketing calls out these periods with the express prior consent of the consumer (that the trader must be able to prove);
* only four times in a 30-calendar-day period to the same consumer, except if the consumer has opposed to this frequency. In this case, the professional cannot call this consumer before a 60-calendar-day period;

* after the call, provide the consumer with the offer on paper or durable medium with a range of specific information;
* use a 10-digit number and not use a hidden number, and in particular not use a number starting by 06 or 07;
* consult on a regular basis, the organism in charge of the do not call list to check the compliance of its marketing list, provided that the professional carries out marketing calls on a regular basis.

 In any case, marketing calls are prohibited for the sale of equipment or work on housing for energy-saving or renewable energy production.

# *Sanctions*

A breach of the rules regarding marketing communications is sanctioned by an administrative fine of up to *75,000 EUR* for a natural person and of up to *375,000 EUR* for a legal person.

 Also, note that the performance of data processing with direct marketing purposes even if the individuals have opposed is sanctioned by up to 5 years imprisonment and a fine of up EUR 300,000.

 But in practice, based on our experience, fines for breach of marketing rules would never reach these amounts and the imprisonment sanction is really theoretical. However, please note that the French data protection authority is more likely to take actions when consumers privacy is at stake, and in case of non-compliance, risks can never be excluded and the amount of the fine would vary depending on several factors such as the seriousness of the breach, the number of data subjects, the turnover of the company, its cooperation with the authorities, etc.

Hi [~accountid:620b5eac156f53006b24766f] regarding this matter please see below a summary:

*Is the cost of the repair the responsibility of the landlord or Bolt?*

In the case of a non-residential tenancy, the law states that the parties can freely decide who is responsible for replacing the door (Art. 1111/1). If the lease agreement is silent, the landlord's responsibility for replacing the door is presumed (Art.1111/2). On this last point, Bolt would only be liable if it was responsible for the damage, which is not the case (Art.1044).

Having analysed the contract, in particular clause SEVENTH - CONSERVATION, CLEANING AND WORKS, it states in the third paragraph that the 1st party, i.e. the landlord, is responsible for carrying out the works essential for the conservation and repair of the structural elements of the rented premises - which is considered to be the entrance door - provided that they are fortuitous and not attributable to BOLT.

Therefore we understand that the +landlord is responsible for repairing the door+.

*Is this justification for terminating the contract?* 

With regard to this question, the law states that the parties can freely agree on the rules relating to the termination of the tenancy agreement (Art. 1110/1). In the absence of a contract with the landlord, the provisions relating to residential tenancy apply, and there is the possibility of terminating the contractual obligations through cancellation and termination (Art. 1079). 

Bolt can terminate the contract due to the landlord's failure to carry out works (which includes replacing the damaged door) that affect the ability to operate the property as provided for in the lease (Art. 1083/5: +The landlord's failure to carry out works for which he is responsible is grounds for termination by the tenant, when such failure jeopardises the habitability of the property and, in general, its suitability for the use provided for in the lease)+.

Termination by the tenant is effected by means of a communication to the counterparty in which the breach of obligation is substantiated. In other words, +a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt must be sent, stating precisely that the obligation to carry out the work falls on the landlord and that this breach is grounds for BOLT, the tenant, to terminate the contract. I will provide a template to be used by the end of the day.+

We recommend you to do a cost-benefit analysis, i.e. what is the value of repairing the door and what is the value of finding a new space and the risk of litigation?  *The risk in terminating the contract in breach of the law is that the landlord initiates a legal action against Bolt requesting the payment of the rents until the end of the 5-year contract*.  This is likely to be a lengthy process and with low prospects of success.

*What is an alternative route?*

An alternative route is for BOLT to +repair the door and then deduct the cost of the repair from the next rent payment+, also sending a +registered letter explaining the reason for doing so+. 

Performing works in the shop requires the prior written authorisation of the landlord, with the exception of urgent repairs.The integrity of the door is an essential element for the security of the premises and therefore falls within the concept of urgent works, and BOLT can carry them out, although the responsibility for payment remains with the landlord.

Please let me know if you have any other questions. Thank you

Thanks - overall, re/ marketing emails and SMS, the requirements are standard ePD Art.13(2), opt out DM is possible. Thus, standard risks that the LCM are already taking apply.

As for the marketing calls (automated/person) - to my knowledge, these happen only in B2B relationships - (BB, merchants in Delivery). These are usually: i) “transactional” (arguably not marketing) with instructions to register; and ii) sales calls to leads (sales/marketing).

However, as the rules are B2C, they should not apply, unless it can be argued that B2B contacts receiving the calls are contacted as individuals (i.e. they use personal, not company, phone number). In this case, it would be a minor risk, as the numbers are official business contact details, and are taken from public sources (i.e. merchants website).

In invoicing there are 3 components to the coupons credit limit:

# {{business_company.vouchers_limit}} - This is how much free credit is *available* for a company.
# {{business_company.balance}} - This is how much money is on the company's balance.
# {{voucher_booking}} rows - Each row in {{BOOKED}} status indicates an active booking/hold of the credit limit.



When a coupon is created:

* If coupon amount > {{vouchers_limit}} + {{balance}} then we don't allow creating coupon
* The {{vouchers_limit}} is decreased.
* A new {{voucherBooking}} is created.

Vice-versa for expired or used coupons.



(For postpaid companies {{credit_limit}} is used in place of {{vouchers_limit}}.)

*_“Стаття 24._* _Адвокатський запит_

# _Адвокатський запит - письмове звернення адвоката до органу державної влади, органу місцевого самоврядування, їх посадових та службових осіб, підприємств, установ і організацій незалежно від форми власності та підпорядкування, громадських об’єднань про надання інформації, копій документів, необхідних адвокату для надання правничої допомоги клієнту._

_До адвокатського запиту додаються посвідчені адвокатом копії свідоцтва про право на заняття адвокатською діяльністю, ордера або доручення органу (установи), уповноваженого законом на надання безоплатної правничої допомоги. Вимагати від адвоката подання разом з адвокатським запитом інших документів забороняється._

_Адвокатський запит не може стосуватися надання консультацій і роз’яснень положень законодавства._

_Надання адвокату інформації та копій документів, отриманих під час здійснення кримінального провадження, здійснюється в порядку, встановленому кримінальним процесуальним законом._

# _Орган державної влади, орган місцевого самоврядування, їх посадові та службові особи, керівники підприємств, установ, організацій, громадських об’єднань, яким направлено адвокатський запит, зобов’язані не пізніше п’яти робочих днів з дня отримання запиту надати адвокату відповідну інформацію, копії документів, крім інформації з обмеженим доступом і копій документів, в яких міститься інформація з обмеженим доступом._

_У разі якщо адвокатський запит стосується надання значного обсягу інформації або потребує пошуку інформації серед значної кількості даних, строк розгляду адвокатського запиту може бути продовжено до двадцяти робочих днів з обґрунтуванням причин такого продовження, про що адвокату письмово повідомляється не пізніше п’яти робочих днів з дня отримання адвокатського запиту._

_У разі якщо задоволення адвокатського запиту передбачає виготовлення копій документів обсягом більш як десять сторінок, адвокат зобов’язаний відшкодувати фактичні витрати на копіювання та друк. I’ve reviewed the [*survey questions*|https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1osuIFpch3EUKqYrAdCsZZjyH5SNwxz7Bi61u_QhCT0U/edit] and categorized these into _High risk_ and _Adjustments needed._

*High risk:*

* *Using data of minors:*

* *Concern:* The question “What is your age?” includes an “Under 18” option. Collecting data from minors usually requires parental consent and has additional restrictions under privacy laws.
* *Proposal:* Remove the “Under 18” option to ensure compliance with privacy laws.

* *Sensitive data collection:*

* *Concern:* Some questions (listed below) involve collecting special category data (sensitive data), which is *prohibited* unless specific exceptions apply (exceptions do not apply in our case).
* *Proposal:* Strongly advise removing these questions to avoid breaching privacy laws:

* “Do you have a disability?”
* “What is your ethnicity?”
* “Are you a member of the LGBTQ+ community?”
* “What is your marital status?”

*Adjustments needed:*

* *Residence-related question:*

* *Concern:* The question “Which country were you born in?” might be challenging to justify under privacy laws, considering the proportionality in the context of a ride-hailing app.
* *Proposal:* Rephrase to “Which country do you reside in?” or “Of which country are you a citizen?” to align better with our objectives, and to make it more proportionate to our goals.

* *Caregiving-related question:*

* *Concern:* While not high risk by default, the question "Do you have any caregiving responsibilities for children or adults?", it would be hard to justify why we collect this information.
* *Proposal:* Unless we have a good reason why we need to know this in the context of a ride-hailing app, I suggest removing this question.

Generally, collecting unnecessary data (data we don't really _need_) or sensitive data (sexual life, health, etc.) exposes us to significant legal risks - that's why we raised this today

Re-opening this file in lieu of further VAT questions raised by tax team:

We are going to keep VAT registered drivers on the platform regardless if they account to HMRC or not, this is the drivers responsibility. 

Bolt UK Driver Platform Terms state at 18(c) that the Journey Fee will be gross of any applicable taxies of similar charges which in my view would be any fee the driver accepted for the journey AND which infers the inclusion of any applicable VAT for their services. Drivers who are VAT registered would therefore receive the gross fare plus VAT. It is assumed that many drivers will earning below the threshold would not be necessarily concerned about the position on receiving a fee that contain VAT. 

Whilst we don't set out precisely everything between the difference between the Fare and Journey Fee, the question remains as to where is it necessary to produce an invoice for those VAT registered drivers showing this?


Analysing what our competitors say on this particular subject matter, Uber has it’s own dedicated webpage to address VAT registration.

[https://www.uber.com/gb/en/drive/tax-information/|https://www.uber.com/gb/en/drive/tax-information/] 

It states mentioned that drivers have a tax profile page that “helps make sure that your invoices are generated correctly”. The webpage provides any general guidance on tax with the usual disclaimers that its not tax advice but does permit driver to “register” their tax status with Uber. It gives the driver the ability to select from the following regimes that may be applicable to the driver:

(1) General VAT Regime

(2) Small-business regime/ below the VAT-registration threshold 

(3) Flat-rate Scheme

There is the assumption that Uber could be providing invoices to certain VAT registered drivers showing their VAT payments as part of the fares so that they can account to HMRC accordingly. 

Ultimately accounting to HMRC for any VAT or tax is the drivers responsibility but there is an argument to suggest that Bolt should be supporting such accounting practice if the services are provided to Bolt and that we are generating the invoices on the Drivers behalf.



Seeking outside confirmation as to whether Bolt should have some responsibility on producing a tax invoice unless the Bolt tax team knows.

Hey Michael ,

In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Currency*: Usually country default if not stated otherwise
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*What is a Base Fee Calculator*

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].

Hi [~accountid:6017bc19dc29b4006a7f1025] - I’m sure that tax team will correct me if I make a misstatement, but a VAT invoice is required when making a chargeable supply to a VAT registered entity (unless an exemption applies either to the service provider or the nature of the supply). Since Bolt is agreeing to issue receipts/invoices on behalf of drivers, Bolt *_should_* provide a VAT invoice - in my view - where we know that the driver / fleet is VAT registered.

There is a commercial question however: does Bolt actually *_want_* to pay out to drivers/fleets on the basis that Journey Fees indicated are stated to be ‘gross of VAT’(regardless of what the terms say)? The impact of this is that it’s culling the -gross- _edit:_ net amount earned by these drivers/fleets by approx. 16.6%. I foresee that this approach would impact the willingness of VAT registered individuals to provide services via our platform.

This is particularly relevant in the context of any existing ‘Bolt Link’ arrangements: we presumably wouldn’t want to discourage any ongoing use of Bolt Link for this reason.

If the cost impact to the business is nominal, perhaps this gives a compelling reason to disregard the T&C on this point - and to assume that journey fees are stated ‘net of VAT’. I do not think the T&Cs ought to lead on this point, even if they are helpful for presenting that journey fees ought to be ‘gross of VAT’.

Ultimately, it probably is worth seeking the opinion of Deloitte etc. on this.

After some investigation it appeared that it’s {{proxysql_syncer.py}} that breaks user sessions.

{{proxysql_syncer.py}} is launched in Screen with 5 min delays between runs.

During the run, the users are deleted first ([https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-39c7ab2398a3877ebb80f879be46da223f49c0b288cf4f7784b664351aff90eaR25|https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-39c7ab2398a3877ebb80f879be46da223f49c0b288cf4f7784b664351aff90eaR25]), and then users found on MySQL masters are added back ([https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-39c7ab2398a3877ebb80f879be46da223f49c0b288cf4f7784b664351aff90eaR26-R40|https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-39c7ab2398a3877ebb80f879be46da223f49c0b288cf4f7784b664351aff90eaR26-R40]). Changes are not committed until all the users are added.

But there are other scripts that manage ProxySQL, for example, {{credentials_applier.py}}. It adds users one by one, and may call ProxySQL’s LOAD?SAVE any time ([https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-3be5e9f94e72fd5a34f57bd0b93b6524ea79e792bab62d4b011e332d7daf0092R239-R240|https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/commit/7a40ad634dc96e8b298afa81fa11474d5f2dd2ad#diff-3be5e9f94e72fd5a34f57bd0b93b6524ea79e792bab62d4b011e332d7daf0092R239-R240]).

So what probably happens is {{DELETE}} and {{INSERT}} user commands are added to ProxySQL by {{proxysql_syncer.py}} but are not committed as the script finds a duplicate user and exists with exception. Also not all the users are added, but only those that are handled before the exception. Then, at some point, {{credentials_applier.py}} runs, makes a user change and commits the pending ProxySQL configs (also those pushed by {{proxysql_syncer.py}}), thus deleting some of the users.

It appears that {{proxysql_syncer.py}} functionality is not needed as users are added to both ProxySQL and MySQL by {{credentials_applier.py}}, so the safest and simplest option is to disable and delete {{proxysql_syncer.py}} completely.

We ran it through with Deloitte and they are good with the approach that VAT is included:

_There is no obligation that a contract goes into the specifics of whether fees are inclusive or exclusive of VAT, however, where a contract doesn’t specify, the consideration is taken to be VAT inclusive._

_Currently the Driver T&Cs themselves don’t make reference to whether journey fees are VAT inclusive or exclusive, but they do cross-reference what is shown in the Driver app (pt 12 defines ‘journey fee’ as “the price paid by Bolt UK to you for the fulfilment of a Journey in association with your account, as indicated to Drivers on the Driver App”)._

_From the Driver Journey screenshots that we included in the hearing evidence, we understand that when a journey is offered to a Driver, it shows a price specified as being ‘net’ (see attached the step we are referring to) – but we understand that is intended to refer to the fee being net of Bolt’s charges, rather than seeking to indicate it is net of any applicable VAT. However, that terminology can be confusing if you intend the journey fee to be gross of VAT and VAT-registered Drivers could well argue that it indicates that VAT should be applied on top of the fee. Therefore, it would be important to make clear to the Drivers that the journey fees they are being offered in the app are_ *_gross of any applicable VAT, but net of Bolt’s charges_*_. Depending on what would be easier to achieve from Bolt’s perspective, it should be fine to either include that clarification in the Driver T&Cs or in the Driver App._

_From a commercial perspective, we’re not sure how you calculate your margin, but if it was calculated as a percentage of journey fee you might need to consider whether that would be the VAT exclusive or inclusive journey fee and make that clear to drivers._

_Another thing to be mindful of with VAT-registered Drivers is periodically checking the validity of any VAT numbers being provided by Drivers and documenting those checks, to help demonstrate that Bolt is complying with its obligations under the Corporate Criminal Offence legislation, given that it will be self-billing on behalf of those Drivers. As referred to in pt 19(ii) of the T&Cs, you should also make sure that Bolt is actually confirming a Driver’s agreement to the self-billing arrangement on an annual basis and is again documenting this._

Original query

**

{noformat}/*
    Spreadsheets coming from https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1EDOe-ZoYDqTe4zuyC6xydUkMzTAvIX8uMNkwxAVWZkg/edit#gid=2125132682
    Ticket where dashboard was developed: MARTECH-5884

    Description:
    This query takes
        daily_spend data,
        model_parameters,
        signup_to_ftr_conversion,
        avg_user_gmv
    and connects them all to one table (using daily_spend data as main key, i.e. left joining to it)
*/


    with daily_spend as (
    Select date_date,
         CASE WHEN country = 'Portugal' then 'Portugal' -- Portugal on the first place ensures it does not become 'Portugal other cities'
         WHEN city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) then city
         WHEN city NOT IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) then concat(country,' other cities')
         end as city,
         country,
         replace(lower(channel_name), ' ads') as channel,
         os as platform,
         sum(metric_value) as cost
    FROM mart_models.mart_rider_ads_metrics
    where  metric_name  = 'Cost'
    and os in ('android', 'ios')
    and date_date between date('2023-01-01') and date_trunc('week', (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1' DAY)) -- dates are only defined here. Taking closest Monday as date on the right
    --and (city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) or country = 'Portugal') -- this is remainder from version before ' other cities'
    and channel_name not in ('Apple Search Brand Ads') -- ASA Brand goes as different budget and follows different decision-making.
    group by 1,2,3,4,5
    order by 1,2,3,4,5),

    model_params as (

    Select *, DATE(LEAD(from_date, 1, date('9999-12-31')) OVER (PARTITION BY city, platform, channel ORDER BY DATE(from_date))) AS end_date
    FROM
      (
      -- modelling
      Select city, platform, channel, DATE(modelling_date) AS from_date,
      vmax_mean, lam_mean, case when has_experiment=1 then 'model+exp' else 'model' end as measurement_state
      from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_mmm_curve_parameters

      UNION ALL
      -- attribution
      Select city, platform, channel, DATE(modelling_date) AS from_date,
      vmax_mean, lam_mean, measurement_state
      from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_attribution_curve_parameters

      )
    ),

    signup_to_ftr_conversion as (

    Select city, platfotm as platform, DATE(date) AS from_date,
    DATE(LEAD(date, 1, date('9999-12-31')) OVER (PARTITION BY city, platfotm ORDER BY DATE(date))) AS end_date,
    conversion_rate
    from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.conversion_signup_to_ftr

    ),

    avg_user_gmv as (
    Select date_date,
          CASE WHEN country = 'Portugal' then 'Portugal' -- Portugal on the first place ensures it does not become 'Portugal other cities'
          WHEN city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) then city
          WHEN city NOT IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) then concat(country,' other cities')
          end as city,
          os as platform,
          sum(case when metric_name ='1Y GMV Eur' then  metric_value else 0 end) / sum(case when metric_name ='First time rides' then  metric_value else 0 end) as AVG_1Y_GMV
    FROM mart_models.mart_rider_ads_metrics
    where  metric_name  in ('1Y GMV Eur', 'First time rides')
    and os in ('android', 'ios')
    --and (city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) or country = 'Portugal') -- this is remainder from version before ' other cities'
    group by 1,2,3
    order by 1,2,3
    ),

    -- collect data from all subqueries and make sure attribution has 100% conversion.
    -- only reason this subquery exists is that we make sure conversion rate is rewritten properly.
    combined_table as (

    select ds.date_date, ds.city, ds.country, ds.channel, ds.platform, vmax_mean, lam_mean, measurement_state,
           CASE WHEN measurement_state = 'attribution' THEN 1 else conversion_rate END AS conversion_rate,
           AVG_1Y_GMV,
           cost

      from daily_spend ds
      left join model_params mp on ds.city = mp.city and ds.channel = mp.channel and ds.platform = mp.platform and (ds.date_date >= mp.from_date and ds.date_date < mp.end_date)
      left join signup_to_ftr_conversion conv on ds.city = conv.city and ds.platform = conv.platform and (ds.date_date >= conv.from_date and ds.date_date < conv.end_date)
      left join avg_user_gmv gmv on ds.date_date = gmv.date_date and ds.city = gmv.city and ds.platform = gmv.platform
      )


    -- calculate metrics
    select date_date, city, country, channel, platform, vmax_mean, lam_mean, measurement_state,
           conversion_rate, AVG_1Y_GMV, -- these two parameters only participate in table calculation, but do not show up themselves (we use measures instead).
           cost,
           vmax_mean*cost / (lam_mean+cost) as signups,
           (conversion_rate) * (vmax_mean*cost / (lam_mean+cost)) as First_Time_Rides_projected,
           (conversion_rate*AVG_1Y_GMV) * (vmax_mean*cost / (lam_mean+cost)) as GMV_projected,
           (conversion_rate*AVG_1Y_GMV) * (vmax_mean*lam_mean) / power(lam_mean+cost, 2) as Uplift_to_cost_ratio_incremental -- Michaelis-Menten derivative

      from combined_table
      order by 1,2,3,4{noformat}

{noformat}    avg_user_gmv as (

      SELECT cl.date_date, cl.city, cl.platform, cl.channel,
      -- 30 is temporary and might be revised later
      -- AVG is set to be able to GROUP BY and ensure we avoid duplicates (even though not expected)
      AVG(CASE WHEN cl.FTRs >= 30 THEN cl.AVG_1Y_GMV ELSE pl.AVG_1Y_GMV END) as AVG_1Y_GMV

      FROM

      -- Query for channel-level granularity
      (
          SELECT date_date,
                CASE WHEN country = 'Portugal' THEN 'Portugal' -- Portugal on the first place ensures it does not become 'Portugal other cities'
                WHEN city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) THEN city
                WHEN city NOT IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) THEN concat(country,' other cities')
                END as city,
                os as platform,
                replace(lower(channel_name), ' ads') as channel,
                SUM(CASE WHEN metric_name ='First time rides' THEN  metric_value else 0 END) as FTRs,
                SUM(CASE WHEN metric_name ='1Y GMV Eur' THEN  metric_value else 0 END) / sum(case when metric_name ='First time rides' THEN  metric_value else 0 END) as AVG_1Y_GMV
          FROM mart_models.mart_rider_ads_metrics
          WHERE  metric_name  IN ('1Y GMV Eur', 'First time rides')
          AND os in ('android', 'ios')
          GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
          ORDER BY 1,2,3,4
      ) as cl -- channel-level

      JOIN

      -- Query for city-platform-level - it should substitute 1Y LTV calculation when channel-level granularity does not have enough observations
      (
          Select date_date,
                CASE WHEN country = 'Portugal' THEN 'Portugal' -- Portugal on the first place ensures it does not become 'Portugal other cities'
                WHEN city IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) THEN city
                WHEN city NOT IN (Select city from ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) THEN concat(country,' other cities')
                end as city,
                os as platform,
                sum(case when metric_name ='1Y GMV Eur' THEN  metric_value else 0 end) / sum(case when metric_name ='First time rides' THEN  metric_value else 0 end) as AVG_1Y_GMV
          FROM mart_models.mart_rider_ads_metrics
          WHERE  metric_name  IN ('1Y GMV Eur', 'First time rides')
          AND os IN ('android', 'ios')
          GROUP BY 1,2,3
          ORDER BY 1,2,3
      ) pl -- platform-level

      ON cl.date_date=pl.date_date AND cl.city=pl.city and cl.platform=pl.platform
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
      ORDER BY 1,2,3,4

    ),{noformat}

* their name, address, telephone number, and e-mail address;

Until we update the article, for further context regarding the confusing bullet point, this is the response we got from Privacy: 

App activity includes:

* *Login Frequency*: How often a user logs in and out from the app.
* *Page Views*: Number of pages or screens viewed in the app.
* *Interaction Types*: Specific actions taken within the app, such as opening a page, getting back to the order screen, opening menu section, opening other sections in the app.
* *Session Length*: The amount of time spent in the app during each visit.
* *Search Queries*: Terms or phrases frequently searched for within the Bolt Food app.
* *Push Notification Response*: How often users receive pushes and how quickly users view the push notifications, whether they close them, how they react.
* *Error Rates*: Frequency of errors or crashes experienced by the user in the app
* *Warnings* the user receives in the app during the ride
* *Devices* used to log in and log out.
* *Logs of changes* made in the app: changing name, surname, phone number or email
* *Abandonment*: Starting but not completing orders within the app, like leaving items in a checkout basket.

Behavioural patterns category is more broad, can be received only from analysis by the respective team of the user's app activity or other parameters and usually include:

* *User preferences:* How frequently the user orders premium or food from a specific merchant, language preferences, marketing preferences
* *High activity of the app usage* during specific times of the day, such as mornings or evenings.
* *Feature Preference*: Regularly using certain features of the app more than others, such as chat between riders-drivers or audio trip recording.
* *Food Search Behavior*: Frequency and type of searches performed within the Bolt Food app
* *Referral or Discount Activity*: Tendency to refer the app to friends or family, tracked through referral codes or links, or using the discounts provided by Bolt.
* *Customization and Personalization*: Use of our features, such as communication preferences or third party data sharing to personalize the app experience or data sharing.

Hope this helps! 🙂

Because if we decide to do table-based access rules, we will have to define those rules for every table separately, more or less.

In a nutshell, Vodacom and Bolt are collaborating to provide preferred payment solutions and access to preferred terms for Vodacom products for Bolt users. It means that passengers and drivers who use the Lipa na M-pesa (pay with M-pesa) solution will get offered discounts by Bolt.  Vodacom will offer preferred lending terms to Bolt registered drivers. 

*This is the proposed DATA flow:*

# *marketing the Lipa na M-pesa (pay with M-pesa) solution to drivers*

* Comms will be sent to all drivers about the partnership with Bolt through sms and in app message
* Vodacom will send sms to their customers about the Lipa na M-pesa solution 
* Direct engagement with drivers at the DEC
* Joint on activation of new drivers
* Social media platforms

# *marketing the Lipa na M-pesa  (pay with M-pesa) solution to passengers*

* In-app comms to Bolt riders
* Social Media
* Joint Media interviews
* Bolt to provide discount for passengers who use the Lipa na M-pesa solution 
Vodacom will share the list of the passengers who have used Lipa kwa Simu to pay for their rides and Bolt will verify the rides and provide discount to the passenger on their next trip

# *data to be shared with Vodacom about interested drivers*

-_Bolt will inform the drivers about the new partnership (where drivers can get some merchant & device financing). For interested drivers, Bolt will share the details with Mpesa._

_For Bolt drivers who go directly to Mpesa, Mpesa will have to reach out to Bolt to confirm whether the said drivers are active Bolt drivers.data to be shared by Vodacom about drivers who have contacted them directly about the Solution._

# *If any google forms are to be used, please share those.*

Vodacom will share reports on:

* Total number of drivers who have requested and successfully received Chomoka and Insurance loan

As a final answer:
There are no legal barriers to processing payments in one territory using a processor located in the country where the card was issued. However, there are contractual limitations. Each time a new market is opened and payments are processed with a PSP (Adyen for example), affiliate agreements or addendums are normally signed to include subsidiaries in the main agreement specific to that territory. The agreements are designed to process payments within a territory, not from one.

Another contractual issue arises with the Terms and Conditions (T&Cs) that vary by country. When using Bolt, customers are bound by the T&Cs of the country they are in, which specify which Bolt entity charges the payment. If a payment is charged by a different Bolt entity not reflected in the T&Cs, it creates a conflict. We are currently working on this issue from the Customer and Driver side, meaning when a Customer moves countries and opens their app, it will show they are now subject to other T&Cs. Same for the Driver who moves to drive from Estonia to Latvia. Also, this is been worked on as part of the Ledger project. 

To address this, it must be confirmed that it is contractually viable by consulting with each PSP we are going to use for this, fix the disclosure of the applicable T&Cs and include new payment terms provisions if necessary (that done from the new Payment terms side).

As discussed the Defenseur des droits reminded us the laws applicable in case of a discrimination which are: 

* article 225-1 Code penal: gives the definition of a discrimination - to resume, treat differently people because of some difference they carry on. 
* article 225-2 Code penal: gives the sanction, i.e. to discriminate someone by refusing a service to them can lead to up to 3 years of imprisonment as well as a fine of up to 45.000 euros.
* article 1 of the law 2008-496 of the 27 May 2008: defines the discrimination.
* article 4 of the law 2008-496 of the 27 May 2008: states that when there is a assumption of discrimination, this will be to the defendant to prove the case (“inversion de la charge de la preuve”).

The code penal relates to criminal law and the criminal jurisdictions. The law 2008-496 relates to civil law and the civil jurisdictions, which are non-exclusive of each other.

*Summary after meeting Max and Ali on 18 June:*

* Fleets can get the data about drivers already through local ops - if a Fleet contacts local ops, they expand their access rights, there are no controls to it. 
* Ali suggestion: we create a *blacklist* and introduce *labelling*
** *Blacklist:* certain types of Fleets (the list of types will be agreed on with Max and Ali) will by default not have access to more data. 
** *Labelling:* in the Fleet portal, we will mark the type of fleet, so that the local teams know if more access can be given or not (the list of types will be agreed on with Max and Ali)
* Fleets have the following traits:
** *attracting leads' signup* - UA "onboarding" fleets case, car financing cases, checking payment details, photos, ensuring activity is tracked on the proper account
** *moving drivers' engagement* - hiring or incentivizing drivers for real, not just on an invoicing strategy level
** {color:#ff5630}*allocating vehicles' usage*{color}{color:#ff5630} - multiple renters, value for carless leads,{color}
** *incentivizing drivers' platform lock* - early cash-outs or other financial support on the grounds of stable & safe commercial activity proofs, rental partnerships with activity conditions to commit on
* That's four traits that are typical for fleets, and for the driver data access, we would give it out to everyone but those with *only* 3rd trait present.
* One problem [statistically, the risk is not high, as most fleets will fall under the “allowed” categories] - once new fleets sign-up, access will be given automatically. Unnecessary access rights will be removed later.

_“ - a premium service designed to help you maximise your earnings”_ - this ought to be revised. 

Ideally, the above wording would be deleted and added to the second paragraph:

* If it’s applying to everyone (fleet and non-fleet drivers): “.. *-allowing-* *_helping_* you to plan your time more effectively *_and fulfil higher value rides_*” :green-check: 
* If it was aimed +_just_+ at independent (non-fleet) drivers: “.. *-allowing-* *_helping_* you to plan your time more effectively *_[_*_option 1:_ *_and maximise your earnings] [_*_option 2:_ *_and fulfil higher value rides]_*.” :green-check: 

Instead of ‘higher value rides’ you could say ‘premium rate rides’ - but you might want to drop the ‘premium’ in the first paragraph.

+*Reasons:*+

* Access to Scheduled Rides (SRs) is going to be locked behind some access to guardrails (cancellation rates etc.) - we need to be mindful of being seen to lock ‘*premium*' tools behind Bolt’s assessment of ‘what is good enough’.
* In addition, this sentence sounds like fluff that isn’t true. Did we _really_ design this to ‘maximise driver earnings’…? If it’s not true, we shouldn’t say it.
* We don’t know how fleet drivers get paid by their fleets - we don’t want to sound like we manage how fleet drivers get paid (hence ‘maximising your earnings’ may not always be appropriate).

Hi Armin, TJ and Raivis

Apologies for the delay in response. The question that was raised is whether the proposed Supply of Contractor Services to Client Terms and Conditions from LHi Group Ltd fall outside of IR35 (which should always be the preference for Bolt). 

Just as a side note, LHi Group Ltd is one the of most “reputable” recruitment agencies in the UK. They are absolutely huge and I would be surprised if they were not operating in compliance with the Agency Workers Regulation 2010. Also note that advising on IR35 is an extremely specialist employment area of law in the UK and not usually conducted by general commercial lawyers (such as GFT field counsels) and we would outsource. 

Fortunately I’ve had some experience of this so can give a general steer but I’m fairly convinced that whilst the LHi Group Ltd terms are favourable to LHi Group Ltd and potentially to the Contractor in terms of getting paid for work conducted, they should not be a problem for Bolt in terms of pushing the candidate outside IR35. 

It is also questionable if they would accept any amendments as our experience of using outside agencies for contractors in the UK do not permit many changes except maybe around solicitation and Introduction provisions so it’s up to the business whether they wish to move forward quickly but I would recommend determining if there is any room for negotiation. 

*Detailed Analysis*
As you know, IR35 is a set of anti-avoidance rules aimed at arrangements that seek to disguise an employee as a self-employed contractor operating via a PSC. If the propose contract is one of employment for tax purposes, IR35 will apply (which is bad for Bolt). 


Armin - you asked some key questions on the roles and responsibilities and I’ve reviewed the terms and made the following conclusions:

(1) This is a fixed term contract for 6 months

(2) The agreement can be terminated by Bolt without cause by giving 1 weeks notice (contrary to Clause 8.3).

(3) The Position Summary & Objective states: _The Senior Sales Operations Manager - Systems role is the face of the sales tools used by the business, responsible for the overall management of the platforms (Salesforce and Groove). They are responsible for leading the team, gathering requirements, designing solutions, and implementing configurations on_ [http://Salesforce.com|http://Salesforce.com|smart-link] _. They develop methodology and best practices for the sales teams, and drive platform adoption of all users. They manage the Salesforce roadmap and all platform initiatives. They will be involved in growth strategy discussions alongside Country Sales Managers, Regional Sales Managers and Head of Sales Operations._

This suggests that the contractor will be highly skilled and that we will be relying on the individual’s expertise to deliver the above. It is unlikely that Bolt cannot and will not control precisely how the above will be delivered given the nature of the role. [~accountid:712020:8da80179-63b1-46f6-976f-5d6ec34a16e0] to confirm this position.

(4) Ideally there would be a provision that states that the contractor should remedy an deficiencies in the work for no additional pay, but this is not present. At Clause 5.3 it states if we are dissatisfied we are still obligated to pay but rely on the termination provision. The fact we can do this with 1 week’s termination is acceptable to Bolt minus any remedial obligation.

(5) It appears that there will be no obligation for Bolt to provide any additional work after the project finishes and the Contractor will not have an obligation to accept any further work given by Bolt. There is no expectation that the engagement will be extended.

(6) The contractor will not receive any corporate benefits from Bolt.

(7) There is a substitution provision at clause 8.6 suggesting that the contractor also does not provide a personal service to Bolt (i.e. they could technically also work for others).

(8) Whilst not ideal the contractor should have limited ability to manage staff and should not really be managed by any of Bolt’s managers, his role does require running team and taking a directors as part of the responsibilities and objectives. I don’t think this is a show stopper.

This is not an in depth analysis and is my high-level view only given the specialism required to clarify the position. However, the above are all indicators of self-employment and on a high level review it would appear that the IR35 risk is low. In addition, the Status Determination Statement and the separate IR35 report produced by LHi Group Ltd would give me confidence that IR35 would not apply in this circumstance.

If you would like me to “mark-up” the terms to further mitigate any risk, I can do so but this will be done on Tuesday next week. We should also find out whether LHi Group Ltd will be amendable to changes. The usual points on liability and being able to make the contractor repeat poor work is key.

* *_Riders don’t have any other option than to pay the driver directly. I mean, literally, pass the banknote to the driver_* *→* This process is for cases when rider reports unpaid trip, this means that they already did not give the money to the driver and probably asking CS what to do. That’s why we have a note for agents that they shouldn’t help the rider settle the payment with the driver. If the rider already agreed with the driver and made a bank transfer or gave cash - then it’s not an unpaid ride case anymore and there’s no issue. 
* *_Rider wants to settle the payment →_* We analyzed this topic with the CXA team and decided that riders shouldn’t pay for their unpaid rides, because:
** We can’t track payments made outside the app. Involving CS as a middleman in such transactions creates complexity, as CS don’t have control over them and can end up in situations where they can’t provide any help.
** Payments outside the app prolong the resolution process, requiring extensive follow-up by CS until both parties confirm payment settlement.
** The driver receives compensation either through automation or manually by CS.
** The rider eventually gets blocked, as not paying for rides violates our rules and we don’t want to allow such riders to continue doing so by letting the rider settle the payment with the driver later.



Thank you for your suggestion, however, we won’t be able to proceed with that. We can revisit this topic if you gather some ticket examples and data showing that the current process is not working properly.

Reopening this ticket to deal with this follow-up question:

{quote}_In Amsterdam as well as other European cities, Airports are pushing for 0-emission transportation and providing benefits to EVs such as dedicated waiting lanes and charging infrastructure. As the majority of our EV drivers are earning less than non-EVs, mainly due to range anxiety and charging times, an opportunity would be to prioritise them in Airport rides. This would give them more predictability in terms of journey distance and charging locations as well as provide them with higher ASP trips.Last time we discussed a general prioritisation of EVs you mentioned this_ [_could pose a reclassification risk_|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/D05MQN31XQD/p1709315773159529] _but I wanted to confirm whether limiting this to a specific venue and considering the common goal of reducing emissions, Airports could be an exceptional case where we can explore some form of prioritisation?_{quote}

Even if it applied in ‘discrete areas’ such as airports, this would still create the same sorts of risk. If Bolt says that one type of person is more entitled to a certain type of (premium) work, then it opens up arguments that all other types of person are negatively affected by Bolt's own 'management of its workforce'.

Our high level ‘rule of thumb’ guidance is that adding prioritisation features will have approximately -30% impact on defending claims (from a starting point of 50:50) - “are drivers prioritised over others, for any reason?” is one of the first questions that we expect we will _have_ to answer to court when any claims are made.

As an aside, NL is the highest risk market for Bolt outside of the markets where we’re already subject to claims. Ditto, all EU markets are going to be subject to increased scrutiny in upcoming years because of the Platform Work Directive. 

For these reasons, prioritisation-related tools are not ideally suited to EU markets and will be shown to add considerable risk during the upcoming de-risking exercises for all markets across 2024/2025.

As a more minor point, Bolt already advertises a ‘first in first out' (FIFO) system in many airports - adding a prioritisation tool would clash with driver expectations / existing FIFO implementations.

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 05 June 2024.

I can’t access the stories screen right now, so I’m just commenting on what I can see via the QR code.

Aside from a couple of recommended tweaks, everything here was fine. Any tweaks / suggestions were made in alignment with the copy content guidance we have live [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide].

The main points:

* where possible and if it accords with our commercial aims, we should use ‘neutral language’ that  applies to both independent drivers *_and_* fleet drivers - sometimes there can be a tension (e.g. we typically don’t know how fleet drivers get paid).
* it’s generally better to promote ‘driver choice / possibilities' than act as if we have done something specifically for the benefit of drivers, as often we do things for our own benefit too!

----

+*Screen 1:*+

!IMG_7770 (b2716adb-1a34-496b-9067-63e00d64ed09).PNG|width=1290,height=2796,alt="IMG_7770.PNG"!

_“ - a premium service designed to help you maximise your earnings”_ - this ought to be revised, if we can do so whilst keeping to our commercial aim 🙏 

Ideally, it would be deleted and we could add very similar wording to the second paragraph:

* assuming that it’s applying to {color:#4c9aff}everyone (fleet and non-fleet drivers){color}: “You can now accept Scheduled Ride requests up to 7 days in advance, *-allowing-* *_helping_* you to plan your time more effectively *_and fulfil higher value rides_*” :green-check: 
* If it was aimed +_just_+ at {color:#4c9aff}independent (non-fleet) drivers{color}: “.. *-allowing-* *_helping_* you to plan your time more effectively *_[_*_option 1:_ *_and maximise your earnings] [_*_option 2:_ *_and fulfil higher value rides]_*.” :green-check: 

Instead of ‘higher value rides’ you could say ‘premium rate rides’ - but you might want to drop the ‘premium’ in the first paragraph.

+*Reasons (FYI):*+

* Access to Scheduled Rides (SRs) is going to be locked behind some access to guardrails (cancellation rates etc.) - we need to be mindful of being seen to lock ‘*premium*' tools behind Bolt’s assessment of ‘what is good enough’.
* Did we _really_ design this to ‘maximise driver earnings’…? As per our golden rules if it’s not true, we shouldn’t say it.
* We don’t know how fleet drivers get paid by their fleets - we don’t want to sound like we manage how fleet drivers get paid (hence ‘maximising your earnings’ not being ideal for fleet drivers). It’s better to use ‘neutral language’, where possible 💪

Hi [~accountid:712020:071fb04b-7e5e-4774-81f6-fd12e7bf404c] 

In short, normally we cannot send SMS to users who we've found via Apollo without their active opt in consent - but this depends on the jurisdiction.

For Poland, opt in consent must be sought both for B2B and B2C promotional/sales comms.

The risks for ignoring this are high in Poland as we have regulatory inquiries on the topic atm + fines are high, and I would not advise proceeding with this.

So, to answer your question:

* no
* no.

Also, on a general note - privacy and LCM functions are collaborating on the topic of cross-pollination in Poland, which concerns your second question.

While a business decision was taken to promote Bolt based on opt out consent (where only opportunity to refuse is given, but no active consent) in Poland, despite the requirement to obtain active opt-in consent, the scope did not include Bolt Business cross-promo to riders.

In theory, you could try to escalate p.2 to the LCM, so this decision would be revisited. But this increases regulatory risks for us further (which are already high), I would highly discourage you from doing this if it's not a critical need for your team. CC [~accountid:6038f479f6ccc000705e716a]

query here:


{noformat}-- CUDDO data
WITH df AS (SELECT 
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_city_campaign_coverage.delivery_discount_rate_1d')AS DOUBLE) dr1,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_city_campaign_coverage.delivery_discount_rate_3d')AS DOUBLE) dr3,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_city_campaign_coverage.delivery_discount_rate_7d')AS DOUBLE) dr7,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.data.delivery_order.total_cost_sharing_by_provider_percentage') AS double) cost_sharing_pct,
COALESCE(CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_delivery_campaign_by_user_phone.avg_campaign_coverage_60d')AS DOUBLE),0) avg_disc_60d,
COALESCE(CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_delivery_campaign_by_user_email.avg_campaign_coverage_60d')AS DOUBLE),0) avg_disc_60d_email,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.query.profiling.fraud_user.count_clean_orders_delivery') AS bigint) count_clean_orders_delivery,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.features.discounts.order_discount_in_eur') AS double) order_disc_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(input, '$.features.discounts.delivery_discount_in_eur') AS double) delivery_disc_eur,
meta.user_id AS user_id,
decision.decision AS decision_text ,
decision.path AS path_text ,
*
FROM archive_analytical.campaign_user_delivery_discount_order c
WHERE TRUE --strategies IS not NULL
AND created_hour >= date'2024-06-01'
)
, temp AS (
    SELECT 
    coalesce(dr1,dr3,dr7) AS CITY_AVG_W_MARGIN,
    avg_disc_60d >= 0.2 OR avg_disc_60d_email >= 0.2c1_avg_disc,
    greatest(avg_disc_60d,avg_disc_60d_email) >= coalesce(dr1,dr3,dr7) + 0.05 AS c2_avg60d_gt_city_margin,
    NOT count_clean_orders_delivery > 0 AS c3_not_good_users,
    NOT cost_sharing_pct >= 80 c4_provider_covered,
    order_disc_eur + delivery_disc_eur AS total_disc_eur,
    * FROM df) 
, FINAL_DF AS (
SELECT 
    c1_avg_disc AND 
    c2_avg60d_gt_city_margin AND 
    c3_not_good_users AND 
    c4_provider_covered  AS CUDDO_PROFILING_PHONE_NUMBER,
    decision_text,path_text,total_disc_eur,
    order_disc_eur,delivery_disc_eur,cost_sharing_pct,
    user_id,
    created_hour FROM temp
ORDER BY 1 DESC
    )
SELECT path_text, decision_text,
DATE(created_hour) DT, count(*), round(SUM(total_disc_eur)) total_disc_eur,
round(SUM(total_disc_eur*cost_sharing_pct/100)) total_disc_providers_eur,
round(SUM(order_disc_eur)) order_disc_eur, round(sum(delivery_disc_eur)) delivery_disc_eur,
avg(cost_sharing_pct) avg_cost_sharing_pct,
count(DISTINCT user_id)
FROM FINAL_DF
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY 1,3{noformat}

*What changes and is relevant to CS:*

* DS won’t be measured by the numbers anymore, as it’s legally risky - _the drivers may ask where did it go_
* Automatic blocking for DS won’t be relevant anymore in the high-risk markets; the Drivers get blocked only after a manual review by the Local OPS. However, this won’t be relevant for low-risk markets and the flow for middle-risk markets hasn’t been decided yet - _we need to clarify this in the article_
* Drivers will be able to select a category promotion (Bronze, Silver, Gold) that gives them certain benefits. For reclassification markets without DS, we use the loyalty version without the Driver Score in place - _I assume we may need an FAQ that sums up how to get the category and how not to lose it, etc_
* Drivers will be able to see compliments _-_ positive reviews by the riders in the app _- drivers may share feedback on it, so the CS should know about the feature_
* We can no longer externally refer to it as "Driver Score" - comms to teams and heads up to quality to check this. Drivers will be blocked only based on the contextual blockings, but never based on a "general blocking".

Note: The old DS setup still stays for some time alongside the A/B test of the revamped version. Once it’s fully rolled out to all the markets, DS will be history.

A/B test: July

*Long answer:*

* Safety contextual guidance is triggered if the CS ticket is closed with any of these tags:

# {{driver_was_speeding}}
# {{driver_held_mobile_device}}
# {{driver_was_smoking}}
# {{driver_road_rage}}
# {{issue_driver_was_visibly_tired}}

* When the drivers try to go online they receive a message saying they need to complete the training.
* Once drivers complete the guidance almost immediately they can go online 

In Driver Score 1, the UI looks like the first screenshot. You can check how the User Stories look [here|https://www.figma.com/design/27vDhz4HXMkzV3kTQMjeCB/Stories-Feature-(Restored)?node-id=2531-16984&t=wcn04ZjvbWtBsoi1-0].

In Driver Score 2, the UI will look like you can see on the second screenshot. The first banner is guidance only, the second one is blocking and re-training. 

Short Answer: These cases don’t have to be escalated to Safety team. The blocking is triggered by Safety signals and no manual actions are required.  Long suspensions are not relevant for Safety signals.
