Hi Venehessa! 🌊 Thank you for raising this request and apologies for the delayed reply. 

* Regarding driver blocks - *please do not* *instruct* OS agents to block drivers if they are unresponsive to our requests about lost items - we don’t have this step in the global process and blocking drivers for such reason could have legal consequences. 
* The process instructs to call the driver, if the driver doesn’t respond - send an outgoing ticket and *wait for 24 hours*, and if there is still no reply we have to follow up with the rider that we could not reach the driver. This means that *the timeframe should not be extended* to more than 24 hours since the agent sent an outgoing ticket. 
* There is a step in the process that asks the agent to tell the rider to contact the authorities in case it’s a valuable item. I would say we should keep this step as simplified as possible, because there are different processes on how to report to the police in different countries and I believe the police will provide the needed instructions to the customers if they decide to report the incident.

I will close this ticket for now, but if you have any questions regarding the above, please let me know 🌻 

Have a great week!

Either party may terminate for convenience, by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt giving not less than two months’ notice.

+Liability of Rollee (Clause 5)+

If Rollee breaches the Agreement then Bolt will be able to claim for direct losses or damages (which will need to be demonstrated).

Damages are capped (for each instance of damage) at the total amount received by Rollee during the six months preceding the event, or the duration of the Agreement thus far if shorter.  Provided that six months elapses, Bolt will be able to claim €30,000 for each damage from Rollee. 

+Bolt’s Obligations (Clause 6)+

Bolt must provide Rollee with all documents, data and information necessary to produce the reports. 

Bolt may not monetise, sell, assign or transfer its rights or obligations, nor the data reports to any third party including affiliates. The data report is not to be copied, arranged, shared or adapted. In other words, the data reports are only to be viewed and used by Bolt. 

+Rollee’s Obligations (Clause 5)+

Rollee must provide the data reports with due care, diligence and following professional standards. 

Rollee is obligated to give their best effort in producing the report, but not to produce a specific result (i.e: specific findings and usefulness not guaranteed).

Rollee does not guarantee the accuracy of the data provided in the report and reliance upon the data is at Bolt’s own risk. 

+Governing Law (Clause 17.5)+

The Agreement is subject to French law and any disputes will fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Paris, France.

Approval is needed as UK Team need Agreements to be under English law with disputes falling under the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

Rollee may use sub-contractors but will notify Bolt of their use and their use does not waive Rollee’s obligations or liability under the Agreement. 

Both parties must keep the existence of the Agreement and the documents and information therein confidential for a period of ten years from the termination of the Agreement.

Hej Cabdulahi, 

*Begäran om tillgång till uppgifter om registrerade - svar* 

Tack för din begäran om tillgång till personuppgifter, som mottogs av oss den 23 maj 2024.

Efter att ha genomfört en noggrann sökning efter register som rör din begäran om tillgång har vi bekräftat att vi behandlar de begärda personuppgifterna. Dataskyddslagstiftningen ger enskilda personer rätt till en kopia av sina personuppgifter inom sökområdet - det vill säga personuppgifter som identifierar dem eller gör det möjligt att identifiera dem utifrån dem som en levande enskild person. 

Som du kanske känner till ger rätten till tillgång enligt dataskyddslagstiftningen inte en enskild person en absolut rätt till fullständig tillgång till alla handlingar som innehåller personuppgifter om honom eller henne. Rätten får t.ex. inte negativt påverka andras rättigheter, inklusive våra affärshemligheter eller immateriella rättigheter och i synnerhet inte den upphovsrätt som skyddar programvaran. Vidare måste vi påpeka att om vi efter noggrann analys kommer fram till att våra rättigheter eller andras rättigheter har företräde, kommer vi inte att kunna ge dig tillgång till viss dokumentation där ett undantag gäller.

Vi delar med oss av kopior av de personuppgifter vi har om dig, inklusive:

* *Orderdata, inklusive plats och tidslinje, skapad vid lokal tid: 24 mars 2024, 22:24:11 (UTC+01:00)*

*Eftersom det också rör sig om tredjepartsobjekt, passagerare, med deras upphämtnings- och avlämningsplatser visade, måste de betraktas som privata och konfidentiella, eftersom de utfärdats i syfte att uppfylla ditt försäkringsbolags begäran i samband med en olycka och du bör endast behandla dessa uppgifter i enlighet med tillämplig sekretesslagstiftning och får inte använda dem på annat sätt, förutom i syfte att uppfylla försäkringsbolagets begäran.*

*Vi vill påpeka att all information som rör tredje part, t.ex. lokaliseringspunkter, inklusive resornas början och slut, normalt inte ingår i de uppgifter som vi delar, såvida vi inte har ett tvingande skäl att åsidosätta detta genom att balansera riskerna med avseende på dina rättigheter.*  

För information om hur vi behandlar relevanta personuppgifter hänvisar vi dig till vår integritetspolicy på [https://bolt.eu/sv-se/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/sv-se/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link]  , som innehåller ytterligare information om:

* De kategorier av personuppgifter som vi behandlar;
* De syften för vilka vi behandlar personuppgifter;
* De mottagare eller kategorier av mottagare till vilka personuppgifterna har lämnats ut eller kommer att lämnas ut;
* De kriterier vi använder för att avgöra hur länge vi ska behålla personuppgifter;
* Källor till personuppgifter som vi erhåller från andra parter;
* Dina rättigheter i förhållande till dina personuppgifter;
* Förekomsten och de förväntade konsekvenserna av automatiserat beslutsfattande/profilering av personuppgifter; och
* Detaljer om eventuell överföring av dina personuppgifter till tredje land eller internationella organisationer och de skyddsåtgärder som används för sådana överföringar.

*Dina rättigheter* 

Utöver din rätt att få tillgång till de personuppgifter vi har om dig har du rätt att begära att vi rättar eller raderar dina personuppgifter, begränsar behandlingen av dina personuppgifter eller invänder mot sådan behandling. Alla sådana förfrågningar som tas emot kommer att beaktas i samband med tillämpliga bestämmelser i relevanta dataskyddslagar. 

Om du är missnöjd med detta svar på din begäran eller med någon annan fråga som rör behandlingen av dina personuppgifter hoppas vi att du fortsätter att samarbeta med oss för att lösa dem. Du har också rätt att klaga direkt till din dataskydds-/tillsynsmyndighet och, beroende på tillämplig dataskyddslagstiftning i ditt land, begära rättslig prövning.

Om du har ytterligare frågor kan du kontakta vår kundtjänst genom att svara på det här e-postmeddelandet.

Med vänlig hälsning,

Bolt

details as (

Under this agreement, the processing of personal data is governed by the roles and responsibilities defined in terms of GDPR compliance. Silverflow acts as the data processor as they will process personal data on behalf of Bolt Ops OU and  Bolt’s instructions regarding such processing. - Bolt Operations OÜ on the other hand acts as the data controller.

Silverflow will handle the data related to payment transactions, which may include personal data of customers, as part of its services (such as authentication, authorization, clearing, and settlement reporting).

Personal data flows from Bolt to Silverflow for processing and then to the payment networks as needed for transaction processing, with Silverflow ensuring secure and compliant handling of the data throughout the process. 

Here is a short description of what the agreement shows: 

# Collection by Bolt - Bolt, acting as the data controller, collects personal data from its customers (payers). This data can include payment information, transaction details, and other relevant customer data. 
# Transmission to Silverflow - Bolt transmits this personal data to Silverflow. This transmission is done through an integration between Bolt’s systems and the Silverflow Platform using the Silverflow API. 
# Processing by Silverflow - Silverflow, acting as the data processor, processes the personal data on behalf of Bolt. The processing activities include authentication, authorization, clearing, and settlement reporting of payment transactions. - Silverflow uses unique transaction references to track individual and multi-scheme payment transactions as they progress through various stages of the payment process. 
# Exchange with Payment Networks - Silverflow facilitates the exchange of data between Bolt and the payment networks (e.g., VISA, Mastercard) required for processing the payment transactions. This data exchange supports transaction steps such as authentication, authorization, and settlement reporting. 
# Reporting and Settlement - The processed transaction data is used to generate reports for settlement purposes. However, Silverflow does not handle the actual settlements; it only facilitates the data exchange necessary for Bolt to interact with its acquirer for settlements. 
# Data Security and Compliance - Throughout this process, Silverflow adheres to the security measures and confidentiality obligations to protect the personal data. Bolt is responsible for ensuring the data passed to Silverflow is accurate and complete. - Both parties ensure compliance with GDPR and other applicable data protection laws, with Bolt as the controller determining the purpose and means of processing and Silverflow following Bolt’s instructions.

Hey [~accountid:615c1af4048360006a44e16c], after careful consideration, we only added to the process that the *claim can be considered false if the rider reports they paid with an unusually large bill compared to the fare*.

Here’s why we won’t be able to add other suggestions:

* *Timeline*: We don't have ticket examples showing that riders tend to report missing change for rides that happened a long time ago. Adding a strict 24/48-hour reporting timeline could negatively impact CSAT, as users might not be able to report the issue immediately but should still receive compensation for missing change. If a rider reports a missing change case that happened a month ago, or at any other illogical time, we expect agents to use common sense and consider this a potential false claim, just as they would with any other report.
* *Checking Graph*: Since agents are not experts in fraud checks, we avoid adding actions related to that and leave this investigation to the Fraud team. Checking the graph would add to the TRT and we don’t want agents to spend additional time on fraud investigations when we have a dedicated team for that.

The note about large bills was already added to the process and if you have further questions, let me know!

Have a nice day. ☀️

Dear Haroon,



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *14 June 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order history*

Since it also relates to a third party subject, a passenger, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Hi all

I reviewed the privacy-related changes, and overall, we received a pushback, but its very inconsistent and does not make sense in my opinion.

They've left a comment clarifying that only the Ukrainian privacy law would apply and thus they would like to keep the existing privacy provisions in section 7.6-7.11, and that they do not accept the DSA. However:

* the agreement itself says in 7.6 that the GDPR applies - it's the original text that they did not remove.
* Moreover - even if the local Ukrainian entity is contracting with the bank in Ukraine, and the payments are processed locally, the Ukrainian entity is effectively not controlling the operations from our side, but the Estonian (EU) operating entity - Bolt Operations OU does. We have a Platform Services Agreement between Bolt Operations OU and the Ukrainian contracting entity, which clarifies that Bolt Operations OU will be responsible for some operations, such as data breach notifications, etc. This leads to the fact that the GDPR will apply to the data processing by the Ukrainian entity. _Internal note - in theory, we can complicate the DSA and clarify that the GDPR will only apply to operations effectively controlled by Bolt Operations OU, but this is unnecessary complication IMO._
* by choice, we choose to comply with the GDPR in Ukraine, as it provides a framework for our privacy operations.

*Overall, I will take some time later this week to summarise the feedback above and share it with the Bank (in Ukrainian), to convince them to accept our provisions.* The DSA and the GDPR compliance threshold should allow us to comply with the Ukrainian law.

The process of collecting payment would happen the same way as we currently work with many companies such a law or corporate firms that arrange trips for clients and staff working on projects for specific clients and charge this back to their clients companies. 

When Web3 book a trip for their customers (passenger) they agree to quoted fee and this is charged directly to the credit card associated on the account, they then arrange payment for this trip from the passenger directly.

Web3’s customers (passenger) will contact them directly with any issues, they will be able to contact their Bolt driver through the tracking link and details provided through Ride Booker but any wider issues will be raised to Web3 and Web3 have agreed they will handle all customer issues with escalations being raised directly to myself. 

We would be unable to collect payments directly from customers because a business account can only have a singular payment method and we do not accept cash in the UK.

Problem Statement: To institute a compulsory practice of incorporating Purchase Orders into all supplier invoices. Currently when invoices are loaded into Workday, we do not see a reference to the Purchase Order number that is included in Telema. Some suppliers are also not incorporating a PO number into the invoices that they send to us. 
{panel}

I think that to break this problem statement up, one part it the business aspect of suppliers inputting the PO number on their invoices, and this has significantly improved in our business, which is good. 

The second part is that *order* field in Telema, is not passed through - it is only utilised for the Bolt Operations OU logic. 

I will describe the solution that I have instructed the technical team to implement: 

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
Add code line to the Telema integration to by default *always* map the +Order+ data in Telema, to be populated into the *External PO Number* field in Workday invoices. 

For Bolt Operations OU, which has current procurement functionality - only allow valid Purchase Orders (i.e. raised via procurement module) and return an error if PO number is not valid. 
{panel}

This logic above will mean that *all* companies, with exception of Bolt Operations OU will have a mapping of Order <> External PO Number. For Bolt Operations, logic will stay as it is. The decision I have taken here, is for the following reasons: 

# We require the PO data as soon as possible, for Romania invoices processing.
# We will require the PO number for any matching with WMS system. 
# We will require the PO number for any order references in countries where we do not have a procurement (Workday) functionality in place, but we will then have visibility of “off-system” POs. 
# The Bolt Operations logic will stay as it is to allow spare parts, and IOT procurement logic. 

Additionally I would like to inform, that the current Telema PO logic for Bolt Operations OU is that *all* the PO lines are copied exactly onto an invoice, with a prepayment dummy line that is then manually input by the accountant. 

Given that we are moving more into supplier invoice processing in Workday, this is already a process that we should look at improving in the near-future - due to the fact that invoices we receive from suppliers should *already* be digitised with exact quantity/amount so that the system can match it against PO lines. This is all part of ongoing improvements and efficiencies in the Accounts Payable and Supplier Invoice Work Area.

WITH trial_balance AS
(
    SELECT CASE
            WHEN memo IN ('EUR RH payouts', 'UA RH Payouts') THEN 'SUBLINE_CAR'
            WHEN memo IN ('EUR FOOD payouts', 'Food payout rejection, correction to AHBT-EE003-23-391362') THEN 'SUBLINE_RESTAURANT' END AS business_line,
           ROUND(SUM(ledger_debit_amount), 2) AS debit,
           ROUND(SUM(ledger_credit_amount), 2) AS credit
    FROM finance_reports.workday_journal_entry_lines
    WHERE ledger_account_id = 1010
      AND company_reference_id = 'EE003'
      AND bank_account_id = 'BOLTEE_CITI_EUR_6810'
      AND DATE_TRUNC('month', accounting_date) = DATE_TRUNC('month', '2024-05-01')
      AND memo IN ('EUR RH payouts', 'EUR FOOD payouts', 'UA RH Payouts', 'Food payout rejection, correction to AHBT-EE003-23-391362')
    GROUP BY 1
),
payout_split AS
(
    SELECT business_line,
           ROUND(SUM(ledger_debit_amount), 2) AS debit,
           ROUND(SUM(ledger_credit_amount), 2) AS credit
    FROM commerce_finance_spark.finance_model_workday_monthly_aggr_tr TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-06-10' tr
    WHERE tr.rs_category = 'PAYOUT_SPLIT'
        AND rs_month_tran_date = DATE_TRUNC('month', '2024-05-01')
        AND region <> 'REGION_GLOBAL'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT tb.business_line,
       tb.debit AS trial_balance_debit,
       tb.credit AS trial_balance_credit,
       ps.debit AS payout_split_debit,
       ps.credit AS payout_split_credit
FROM payout_split ps
LEFT JOIN trial_balance tb ON ps.business_line = tb.business_line

hey all. 

I’ve had a call with Mário and Carolina to discuss this topic. 

summary of the call: 

* we discussed the risks of the category. it was agreed that it’s high-risk due to the following reasons that can be exploited by fraudsters:
** Fraud won’t have a lot of control in terms of the destination changes that happen during the ride. we won’t be able to apply our usual dest change rules or we would kill the purpose of the category. at max, we could consider capping the number of destination changes per order, which wouldn’t be enough to prevent fraudsters from boosting the order price to cash out. 
** in addition to not having control over the allowed dest changes, Fraud wouldn’t have control over ending the ride. fraudsters could easily turn the ride into hundreds of euros by keeping it active for hours. 
*** advised that they could reach out to Pricing to check if they offer any assistance in regards to ending a ride after a certain threshold. something similar to what we have on Micromobility where we end a ride once it reaches the preauth amount. 
* Carolina suggested enforcing the T&C to execute refunds if we’re unable to capture the funds from the customer on longer rides. 
** advised them to reach out to Legal about this topic. I assume there’s very little chance that Legal will support this, but if they do by any chance, Fraud would assist in performing the refunds. would probably need to create a manual process, as automatic refunds aren’t allowed by PT regulation. 

in a few words, Fraud won’t be able to assist much in reducing risk and limiting losses due to the lack of available tools in our system. if the local team does decide to launch the category anyway, I’ve advised them to keep a close eye on it before it gets out of hand.

Hi Helen, hi Stanislas,

We wanted to organise a meeting to more efficiently address the amendments you've proposed to our General Terms and Conditions.

As Nacho previously communicated, our GTCs, similar to yours, are non-negotiable and universally applicable to all users of our platform. Therefore, we cannot modify them for a specific client. However, given our interest in establishing a long-term commercial relationship and offering you favorable terms, we are open to making the transport commission contract the primary binding agreement between us, superseding our GTCs.

As such and after reviewing your proposed amendments, the following points are problematic for us:

* *Article 4.3:* We cannot guarantee specific departure or arrival dates due to the unpredictable nature of the logistics sector. While we strive to adhere to these dates, they can only be estimates.
* *Article 7.1:* We cannot delete the clause regarding price variation after a quotation has been accepted due to the fluctuating nature of the logistics industry. Our suppliers’ prices can sometimes vary significantly, and the initial quotation may become outdated. Additionally, specific events such as customs controls can lead to substantial surcharges. It is a standard legal practice for transport commissioners to invoice clients for any surcharges from suppliers (e.g., fuel price or freight rate variations). Moreover, we reserve the right to adjust our prices if essential information provided by our clients changes after a quotation has been accepted (e.g., changes in weight or nature of services requested, which affect the commercial dynamics).
* *Article 9.3:* We cannot remove the legally set cap for our liability in the event of a substitute’s fault. While we assume responsibility for our substitutes’ actions, this is limited to the extent of their own assumed liability.



To progress towards finalising this commercial relationship, we would also need to expand the scope of the contract to be more comprehensive, covering aspects such as pricing and liability risks, to reflect the parties' intentions and maintain contractual balance.

Please let me know if these points are acceptable to you so we can start working on amending the contract accordingly.

*B. * Bolt is +*not*+ under a legal obligation to provide DOB information to Wise, as Bolt is is not regarded as a financially regulated entity. However, if Bolt fails to provide the data / cooperate with Wise, Wise reserves the right to stop processing payments for Bolt.

** Updated Thoughts **

* *Data minimisation:* No change. Data sharing does not seem overly intrusive.
* *Legal basis:* Legitimate interest appears to be the applicable legal basis (consent would be impractical; sharing is not strictly necessary for perform contract between Bolt and users; not due to a legal obligation). As such, a +legitimate interest assessment+ will be needed.

* *Agreement:* TBC with Cesar whether the linked agreement applies to this arrangement. If it does, then this looks sufficient (i.e., nothing further needed):
** Confirms that the parties are acting as independent controllers and will comply with applicable laws.
** Requires the parties to cooperate and notify each other of a relevant personal data breach within one business day.
** Requires parties to execute a DPA if so required.
** Does not contain international transfer mechanisms, but these are not required (both parties are in the EEA).
